rows.name: Parallel agents in worktrees
rows.offer: Runs many coding agents side by side, each task in its own git worktree and branch.

flisk.reason: Flisk runs the services agents work against, not the agents or their worktrees; a workspace manager is an ADE job.

rows.name: Works with any CLI agent
rows.offer: Launches and tracks any terminal coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and others) plus custom ones.

flisk.reason: Flisk does not launch agents, but any agent that can run shell commands or speak MCP can drive it.

text.contains: Any other agent that can run terminal commands works too

rows.name: MCP server for agents
rows.offer: Exposes tasks, workspaces, terminals, pages and automations to other agents over a hosted MCP server.

rows.name: Skills agents get automatically
rows.offer: Ships skills that teach agents to set up a repo, orchestrate, automate, diagnose and file feedback, installed with the app or via npx skills.

rows.name: Agent makes repo ready
rows.offer: A setup skill has the agent author the project config and scripts, then verifies them in a real workspace.

flisk.reason: Flisk scaffolds a project and its skills with one command, but it has no agent-authored setup that is then verified end to end.

text.contains: `flisk project` writes the Flisk skills to `.claude/skills/`

rows.name: Diagnose problems skill
rows.offer: A doctor skill finds expired auth, offline hosts and stale versions and fixes them one step at a time.

rows.name: Running state per workspace
rows.offer: Shows running agents, open ports and PR state inline on each workspace in the sidebar.

rows.name: Port discovery and management
rows.offer: Discovers listening ports per workspace, lets you open or kill their process, and labels them from a committed ports file.

rows.name: Restartable run command
rows.offer: A Run button starts long-lived dev commands in a dedicated pane that can be stopped and restarted without recreating the workspace.

rows.name: Setup and teardown scripts
rows.offer: Runs project-defined commands in order when a workspace is created or deleted, with per-user overrides.

flisk.reason: Flisk has no user-defined pre-up or post-down commands; one-off steps like migrations are meant to be a migrator resource, but a small hook list could cover env copying and cleanup.

rows.acceptance: A documented hooks key in service.json or the project config, proved by a file under docs/ and an up/down test in cli/src/commands/__tests__ that runs it.

ice.basis: impact: migrator resources already cover the main use, so only env-copy and cleanup chores gain; confidence: setup scripts are documented well but Flisk's workaround is real; ease: needs a new manifest field plus up.ts and down.ts wiring and schema docs.

rows.name: Agent attention notifications
rows.offer: Notifies you with sound and dock badge when an agent finishes or waits for your input.

flisk.reason: A desktop or terminal notice when flisk up becomes ready or a resource turns unhealthy would help people who tab away while a stack boots.

rows.acceptance: flisk up or status --watch emits a notification, shown by a file under docs/ and a test in cli/src/commands/__tests__ for the ready and unhealthy cases.

ice.basis: impact: waiting on a slow boot is a common annoyance but not a blocker; confidence: Paradev notifies on agent state, not service health, so the mapping is indirect; ease: no notification code exists in the CLI outside the MCP server, so it needs a new cross-platform path.

rows.name: Resume, fork and hand off sessions
rows.offer: Resumes crashed agent sessions automatically and can fork a session or pass its context to another agent.

flisk.reason: Flisk agent resources keep checkpoints that survive restarts and can be listed and read, but there is no fork or hand-off.

rows.name: Parallel isolated environments
rows.offer: Gives each task its own workspace with its own directory, terminals and ports so many can run at once.

flisk.reason: Flisk picks collision-free host ports from bounded ranges, but running one project from several worktrees at once is not a documented workflow.

text.contains: Flisk selects host ports from bounded fallback ranges

rows.name: Coordinator agent fans out work
rows.offer: A skill lets one agent create workspaces and run worker agents, reading their terminals and verifying results.

flisk.reason: Coordinating several coding agents across worktrees is workspace management, not something a local service runtime does.

rows.name: Scheduled and event automations
rows.offer: Starts agent sessions on a schedule or from GitHub, Slack, Linear, Sentry, Notion, Teams or webhook events (Pro).

flisk.reason: A hosted trigger service that dispatches agent runs belongs to a control plane, which Flisk deliberately is not.

rows.name: Cloud workspaces
rows.offer: Runs workspaces in cloud sandboxes from per-repo environments so agents continue with the laptop closed (early access).

flisk.reason: Flisk is local by design and does not host sandboxes.

rows.name: Remote access through a relay
rows.offer: Reaches workspaces on another machine through a hosted relay, with forwarded ports.

flisk.reason: Flisk runs on the machine in front of you; reaching other hosts is a hosted-service concern.

rows.name: In-app browser and design mode
rows.offer: A built-in browser previews running services and lets you click an element to send its DOM, styles and screenshot to an agent.

flisk.reason: Flisk is a CLI and runtime with no GUI workspace; it does expose service URLs through status.

rows.name: Diff viewer and PR pane
rows.offer: Reviews changes, commits, pushes and merges pull requests with checks and review threads from one dashboard.

flisk.reason: Code review is a git host and IDE job, not a local runtime job.

rows.name: Shareable agent Pages
rows.offer: Agents publish HTML reports as shareable pages with version history and pinned team comments.

flisk.reason: Publishing and commenting on documents is a hosted collaboration product outside a local runtime.

rows.name: Persistent terminals
rows.offer: Terminals live in a background daemon so agents keep running after the app closes and reattach with scrollback.

flisk.reason: Flisk is not a terminal emulator; its services already keep running under Tilt or Docker.

rows.name: Mobile app for agents
rows.offer: An iPhone and iPad app to check on agents, reply and review diffs, with Live Activities.

flisk.reason: A mobile client is a hosted product surface that does not fit a local CLI.

rows.name: Computer control
rows.offer: Lets agents operate native desktop apps through an accessibility-first driver.

flisk.reason: Desktop automation is an agent capability, not a service runtime feature.

rows.name: SOC 2, SSO, SCIM and audit logs
rows.offer: Offers a SOC 2 Type II audited service plus SSO, SCIM, audit logs and an SLA on the Enterprise plan.

flisk.reason: Flisk is a local open-source tool with no hosted account, so tenant-level enterprise controls do not apply.
